mainTopic: Waiting periods for a נזיר with mixed doubtful and definite טומאה and צרעת, and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's teaching that one shaving cannot count for both a נזיר and a מצורע.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the condition a doubtful נזיר says over his עולה. If he was simply a pure נזיר, the first עולה was the required one and this one is a gift. If he was טמא and a confirmed מצורע, this one is the required one. Next the גמרא lists three cases that mix doubtful or definite טומאת מת with doubtful or definite צרעת. For each case it says when he may eat קדשים and when he may drink wine and become טמא למת. Then רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's students ask whether a נזיר who is also a מצורע can shave once and have it count for both. He says no. The students suggest one pairing of shavings after another. Each time he points to a difference: removing hair versus growing it, shaving before versus after זריקת דמים, and shaving before versus after immersion. The amud ends with his summary of why no single shaving can serve both statuses.

steps.title: Finishing the condition on the burnt-offering
steps.stepSummary: The doubtful נזיר states a condition so each עולה counts as whatever it needs to be. If he was simply a נזיר, the first עולה was the חובה and this one is a נדבה. If he was טמא and a מוחלט, the first was a נדבה, this one is the חובה, and the other offerings complete his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he really was just a regular נזיר, the first burnt-offering was the one he owed, and this one is a voluntary gift. If he was impure and a confirmed leper, the first one was the gift, this one is the one he owes, and these other offerings are the rest of what he owes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the condition the doubtful נזיר says out loud when he brings his burnt-offering. This closes its explanation of the earlier case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nobody knows which status he really had, he cannot simply label each offering. So he says: whichever status turns out to be true, let each offering count as what that status needs. Either way, nothing he brings is wasted or misused.

keyTerms.meaning: Definitely, for certain
Burnt-offering, burned entirely on the מזבח
An obligatory offering, one he owes
A voluntary gift offering
A confirmed מצורע, declared definitely leprous by a כהן
The rest of his required offerings

steps.whatToRemember: A person in doubt can bring offerings with a condition, so each one counts as whatever the true situation requires.

phrases.english: And if he is definitely just a nazirite —
the first burnt-offering was the required one,
and this one is a voluntary gift.
And if he is impure and a confirmed leper —
the first burnt-offering was a gift,
and this one is the required one,
and these are the rest of his offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the conditional statement from the earlier part of the סוגיא, before this section begins.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With a spoken condition, the doubtful נזיר's offerings are correctly assigned whatever his true status was.

steps.title: Possibly impure, definitely a confirmed leper
steps.stepSummary: A נזיר who is a ספק טמא מת but a definite מוחלט may eat קדשים after 8 days. He may drink wine and become טמא למת only after 67 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is uncertain whether he became impure from a dead body, but he is definitely a confirmed leper, he eats sacrificial food after eight days. He drinks wine and becomes impure from the dead after sixty-seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new list of related cases. This first case mixes a doubtful טומאת מת with a definite צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 8 days come from purifying from צרעת: 7 days of counting, then offerings on the 8th, after which he may eat קדשים. Ending his נזירות takes longer, 7 + 30 + 30 = 67, because he counts a second 30 in case his first נזירות counting was really for his impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: Doubtful, uncertain
Eats sacrificial food
Drinks wine, which a נזיר may do only after finishing his נזירות
Becomes impure from the dead, also allowed only after his נזירות is over

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate deadlines. Eating קדשים depends on finishing the צרעת purification. Wine and contact with the dead depend on finishing the נזירות. Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: One who is possibly impure and definitely a confirmed leper —
phrases.notes: "Impure" here means impure from a dead body.

phrases.english: eats sacrificial food
after eight days,
and drinks wine and becomes impure from the dead
after sixty-seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the earlier case, the גמרא opens a list of similar mixed-status cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doubtful טמא, definite מוחלט: he may eat קדשים after 8 days, and drink wine and become טמא למת after 67 days.

steps.title: Possibly a confirmed leper, definitely impure
steps.stepSummary: A נזיר who is a doubtful מוחלט but definitely טמא מת may eat קדשים after 37 days. He may drink wine and become טמא למת only after 74 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is uncertain whether he is a confirmed leper, but he is definitely impure from a dead body, he eats sacrificial food after thirty-seven days. He drinks wine and becomes impure from the dead after seventy-four days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reverse case: now the צרעת is doubtful and the טומאת מת is certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He first deals with his definite impurity (7 days), then counts 30 days of נזירות. That brings him to 37, when he may eat קדשים. Finishing his נזירות takes much longer (74), because in case he really was a leper, his earlier shavings are used up on the leper purification, so he needs extra counting.

keyTerms.meaning: Possibly a confirmed מצורע
Definitely impure from a dead body
Thirty-seven
Seventy-four

phrases.english: One who is possibly a confirmed leper and definitely impure —
eats sacrificial food
after thirty-seven days,
and drinks wine and becomes impure from the dead
after seventy-four days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 2: the doubtful and definite statuses are switched.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doubtful מוחלט, definite טמא: he may eat קדשים after 37 days, and drink wine and become טמא למת after 74 days.

steps.title: Definitely impure and definitely a confirmed leper
steps.stepSummary: A נזיר who is definitely טמא מת and definitely a מוחלט may eat קדשים after 8 days. He may drink wine and become טמא למת after 44 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is definitely impure from a dead body and definitely a confirmed leper, he eats sacrificial food after eight days. He drinks wine and becomes impure from the dead after forty-four days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last case, where both statuses are certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because nothing is in doubt, he needs no extra counting to cover himself. He finishes the צרעת purification (7 days, then eating on the 8th). Then he does 7 days for the טומאת מת and 30 days of pure נזירות: 7 + 7 + 30 = 44.

keyTerms.meaning: And definitely a confirmed מצורע
Eight days
Forty-four

steps.whatToRemember: Doubt makes the waiting longer. When both statuses are certain (44 days), he finishes sooner than in either case that has a doubt (67 or 74 days), because certainty means no extra counting just to be safe.

phrases.english: One who is definitely impure and definitely a confirmed leper —
eats sacrificial food
after eight days,
and drinks wine and becomes impure from the dead
after forty-four days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the set of cases by taking the one where both statuses are certain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Definite טמא and definite מוחלט: he may eat קדשים after 8 days, and drink wine and become טמא למת after 44 days.

steps.title: Can one shaving serve both the נזיר and the מצורע?
steps.stepSummary: The students ask רבי שמעון בן יוחאי whether a טהור נזיר who is also a מצורע can shave once and have it count for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students asked רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: a pure נזיר who is also a מצורע, may he shave one time and have it count for both?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a question that students put to רבי שמעון בן יוחאי. They ask about a person who must shave both as a נזיר and as a מצורע: is one shaving enough?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר טהור shaves when his נזירות ends, and a מצורע shaves as part of his purification. The students are asking whether one act of shaving can fulfill both obligations at once.

keyTerms.meaning: his students
a נזיר who stayed pure and completed his term
a person with the skin affliction צרעת
a shaving
for this and for that, meaning for both

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: His students asked Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
A pure nazir who is also a leper,
what is the law: may he shave one shaving
and it counts for him for this and for that?
phrases.notes: "This and that" means his נזירות shaving and his צרעת shaving.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the doubtful-נזיר rulings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one shaving can count for both the נזיר and the מצורע obligations.

steps.title: He may not shave once for both
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי answers that one shaving does not count for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: he does not shave once for both.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי gives a short answer: no, one shaving cannot cover both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He has not yet given a reason. The students will ask why in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: he does not shave, meaning not once for both

phrases.english: He said to them: He may not shave once for both.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One shaving does not count for both.

steps.title: Reason: one shaving removes hair, the other grows it
steps.stepSummary: Asked why, he explains that the נזיר shaves to remove hair, while the מצורע's shaving is meant to let hair grow back.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked why. He said: if both shavings were to grow hair, or both were to remove hair, you would be right. But the נזיר shaves to remove his hair, and the מצורע shaves so that hair will grow back.
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask for the reason, and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי explains that the two shavings have opposite purposes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נזיר's shaving ends his נזירות, so its goal is simply to remove the hair. The מצורע's first shaving is followed by another shaving seven days later, so its goal is for the hair to grow back for that later shaving. Shavings with opposite goals cannot be combined.

keyTerms.meaning: to grow, meaning the hair should grow back
to remove the hair
you would be speaking well, meaning your idea would be right

phrases.english: They said to him: Why?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: אִילּוּ זֶה לְגַדֵּל וְזֶה לְגַדֵּל,
phrases.english: He said to them: If this one were to grow hair and that one were to grow hair,
or this one were to remove hair and that one were to remove hair,
you would be speaking well.
Now, a nazir shaves to remove his hair,
and a leper shaves to grow hair.
phrases.notes: He means the מצורע's first shaving, which comes before a second shaving seven days later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the ruling of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two shavings have opposite purposes, removing hair versus growing it.

steps.title: Then let it count for his second, later shaving
steps.stepSummary: The students push back: even if it can't match the first מצורע shaving, let it match the second one, which is also meant to remove hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, let it not count for the end of his confirmed צרעת, but let it count for the end of his days of counting!
steps.whatsHappening: The students challenge his reasoning. They point to the מצורע's second shaving, which is also a 'removing' shaving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'grow vs. remove' difference only applies to the מצורע's first shaving. The shaving at the end of the seven counting days has no further shaving after it, so it removes hair, just like the נזיר's. The students argue that this one should be able to match.

keyTerms.meaning: his days of confirmed צרעת; the first shaving comes when they end
his seven days of counting; the second shaving comes when they end

phrases.english: Let it not count for him for his days of confirmed leprosy,
but let it count for him for his days of counting!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the request to avoid the problem raised in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason given in step 7, which seems to cover only the first מצורע shaving.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second מצורע shaving also removes hair, so the purpose difference does not apply to it.

steps.title: Difference in timing: before or after the blood
steps.stepSummary: He answers that the מצורע shaves before the blood of his offerings is sprinkled, while the נזיר shaves after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: if both were before the sprinkling of the blood, you would be right. But a מצורע shaves before the blood is sprinkled, and a נזיר after.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי answers with a new difference, this time about when each shaving happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצורע shaves on day seven, before his offerings are brought. The נזיר טהור shaves after the blood of his offering has been sprinkled. Since they happen at different points in the process, one shaving cannot serve both.

keyTerms.meaning: sprinkling the blood of the offerings on the מזבח
before
after

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לָהֶן: אִילּוּ זֶה לִפְנֵי זְרִיקַת דָּמִים
phrases.english: And he said to them: If this one were before the sprinkling of the blood
and that one were before the sprinkling of the blood,
you would be speaking well,
but a leper shaves before the sprinkling of the blood,
and a nazir shaves after the sprinkling of the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר לָהֶן: אִילּוּ זֶה לִפְנֵי זְרִיקַת דָּמִים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both shavings remove hair, so they should be able to combine.
steps.terutzMaskana: They still differ in timing relative to זריקת דמים, so they cannot combine.

steps.title: Then pair the מצורע with an impure נזיר's shaving
steps.stepSummary: The students suggest pairing the מצורע's shaving with the shaving of a נזיר טמא, which also comes before the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, let it not count for his צרעת and his pure נזירות, but let it count for his צרעת and his טומאה shaving!
steps.whatsHappening: The students try again. They look for a נזיר shaving that also comes before the blood, and they point to the shaving of a נזיר who became טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר טמא shaves on his seventh day and brings his offerings on the eighth. So his shaving, like the מצורע's, comes before זריקת דמים, and the timing problem from step 9 seems to go away.

keyTerms.meaning: his צרעת
his נזירות, here meaning the pure נזיר's shaving
his טומאה, meaning the shaving of a נזיר who became טמא

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא תַּעֲלֶה לוֹ לִימֵי צָרַעְתּוֹ וּנְזִירוּתוֹ,
phrases.english: Let it not count for him for his leprosy and his naziriteship,
but let it count for him for his leprosy and his impurity!
phrases.notes: "His impurity" means the shaving a נזיר does when he becomes טמא, which also comes before his offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא תַּעֲלֶה לוֹ לִימֵי צָרַעְתּוֹ וּנְזִירוּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds a נזיר shaving that avoids the timing difference of step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The נזיר טמא's shaving also comes before the blood, so it should match the מצורע's.

steps.title: Difference in timing: before or after immersion
steps.stepSummary: He answers that the נזיר טמא shaves after immersing in water, while the מצורע shaves before immersing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: if both were before immersion, you would be right. But the טמא shaves after immersion, and the מצורע shaves before immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי gives a third difference, this time based on immersion in a מקוה. The students will push back once more in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the shaving of a נזיר טמא does not match the מצורע's. The טמא shaves after he has immersed, while the מצורע shaves and only then immerses. So this pairing fails too, though the students will try one more pairing in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'entering water', meaning immersion in a מקוה
here, a נזיר who became טמא

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: אִילּוּ זֶה לִפְנֵי בִּיאַת מַיִם
phrases.english: He said to them: If this one were before immersion in water
and that one were before immersion in water,
you would be speaking well.
But an impure nazir shaves after immersion in water,
while a leper shaves before immersion in water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: אִילּוּ זֶה לִפְנֵי בִּיאַת מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10; the students respond with another pairing in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The נזיר טמא and the מצורע both shave before the blood, so they should be able to combine.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ relative to immersion, so one shaving still cannot count for both.

steps.title: The students concede one pairing but propose another
steps.stepSummary: The students agree the shaving can't count for the מצורע's counting days and the pure נזיר. But they argue it should count for the end of the confirmed צרעת and for the impure נזיר, since both shavings are meant to let hair grow.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You spoke well that it should not count for his days of counting and his נזירות. But let it count for his days of confirmed צרעת and his טומאה, since this one is to grow hair and that one is to grow hair!
steps.whatsHappening: The students accept that the מצורע's counting-days shaving cannot pair with the pure נזיר's shaving, as answered in step 9. Then they push back with a new pairing: the מצורע's first shaving together with the shaving of an impure נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students admit the pure נזיר's shaving and the מצורע's later shaving really are different. Now they match the shavings by purpose. The מצורע's first shaving (ending the חלוט period) and the impure נזיר's shaving are both done so hair will grow back. So why not let one shaving cover both?

keyTerms.meaning: You spoke well: agreeing with part of what was said before pushing further
His days of counting: the seven days a מצורע counts after he is healed
His confirmed צרעת: the period when the כהן has declared him definitely a מצורע
His impurity: here it means his status as an impure נזיר
To grow: a shaving done so that new hair grows back

phrases.english: They said to him: You have spoken well
that it should not count for him
for the days of his counting and for his נזירות,
phrases.notes: This is the pairing from step 8 that step 9 turned down: the מצורע's later shaving with the pure נזיר's shaving.

phrases.english: but let it count for him
for the days of his confirmed צרעת and his impurity,
since this one is to grow hair and that one is to grow hair!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the earlier distinctions and offers a new pairing of shavings based on a shared purpose.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's claim that no single shaving can serve both the נזיר and the מצורע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מצורע's first shaving and the impure נזיר's shaving share the same purpose (letting hair grow), so they should be combinable.

steps.title: Two differences block every pairing
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי sums up both differences. A pure נזיר shaves to remove hair, while the מצורע shaves to grow it. An impure נזיר shaves after immersing in water, while the מצורע shaves before.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: A pure נזיר who is also a מצורע: this shaving is to grow and that one is to remove. And if it is an impure נזיר who is also a מצורע: this one is before immersion in water and that one is after immersion in water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחי answers by putting both differences side by side. Each kind of נזיר is different from the מצורע in its own way, so no shaving can be shared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Against the pure נזיר, the purpose is different: the מצורע shaves to grow hair, the נזיר to remove it. Against the impure נזיר, the purpose matches, but the timing does not. The מצורע shaves before immersing, the impure נזיר after. One mismatch is enough to stop the shavings from combining.

keyTerms.meaning: To remove: a shaving done to take the hair away, not to let it regrow
Entering water: immersing in a מקוה
A pure נזיר: one who finishes his נזירות in purity
An impure נזיר: one who became impure from a dead body during his נזירות

steps.whatToRemember: No shaving can serve both a נזיר and a מצורע. With a pure נזיר the purpose differs (remove vs. grow). With an impure נזיר the timing differs (after immersion vs. before).
steps.confusionAlert: In this answer, 'זה' (this) refers to the מצורע and the second 'זה' (that) refers to the נזיר. Don't flip them: the מצורע grows hair and shaves before immersion.

phrases.english: He said to them:
A pure נזיר who is also a מצורע:
this one is to grow hair and that one is to remove it,
and if it is an impure נזיר who is also a מצורע:
this one is before immersion in water
and that one is after immersion in water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: נָזִיר טָהוֹר וְהוּא מְצוֹרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the new pairing by restating the timing difference and combining it with the earlier purpose difference.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: shows a mismatch in timing even where the purpose matches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both the מצורע's first shaving and the impure נזיר's shaving are meant to grow hair, they could count as one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Shared purpose is not enough; the different timing relative to immersion keeps them separate, so one shaving never counts for both.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes רבי שמעון בן יוחי's argument: a נזיר who is also a מצורע must do separate shavings for each status.
